title: Wind, Water and Ice
objective: After this level you can explain how erosion carves canyons, valleys and coastlines.
summary: Weathering breaks rock down; erosion carries it away. Water carved the Grand Canyon, glaciers grind U-shaped valleys, waves cut arches and stacks, and wind shapes dunes.

cards.headline: The Grand Canyon was dug by a river.
cards.body: No colliding plates, no volcano. The Colorado River started carving about 5 to 6 million years ago, and the canyon is now about 1.6 km deep.

cards.headline: Break it, then move it
cards.body: Two jobs shape the land. Weathering breaks down or dissolves rock where it sits. Erosion wears material away and carries it off, and liquid water is the biggest carrier on Earth. The Colorado River had help: in floods it hauls large rocks that act like chisels, chipping pieces off its own bed. Wind and glacial ice erode, too.

mascot.line: These two get swapped a lot. Weathering breaks rock where it sits; erosion carries it away.

cards.headline: V for river, U for ice
cards.body: Remember Level 7's valleys? Rivers cut them into a V. Glaciers grind them into a wide U. And the eroded bits have to land somewhere: where a river slows at its mouth, it drops its sediment and builds a delta. Erosion doesn't destroy land so much as move it.

cards.headline: Coasts and deserts
cards.body: At the coast, waves bore caves into cliffs. When a cave breaks through, it becomes an arch; keep the waves coming and you're left with rock columns called sea stacks. In deserts, wind does the carving, sculpting rock and piling sand into dunes. Same job, different tools.

cards.headline: Erosion: at work
learned: Weathering breaks rock; erosion carries it away
Water is the main agent: the Grand Canyon
Rivers cut V valleys, glaciers grind U valleys

questions.prompt: Match each term with what it does or leaves behind.

pairs.right: Wears material away and carries it off

questions.explanation: Weathering breaks down or dissolves rock where it sits. Erosion wears material away and carries it off. Glaciers grind valleys into a wide U.

questions.prompt: Waves that hollow a cave into a sea cliff until it breaks through have made _____.

options.label: a delta
options.rationale: A delta is built from river sediment.

questions.explanation: When a wave-cut cave breaks through, it becomes an arch. More erosion leaves sea stacks.

questions.prompt: From Level 7: a valley has a wide U shape. What most likely carved it?

options.label: Wind
options.rationale: Wind shapes rock and dunes, not deep valleys.

options.label: Ocean waves
options.rationale: Waves carve coasts: caves, arches and stacks.
